title: On the Increase of Boltzmann Entropy in Closed Macroscopic Quantum Systems
abstract: We consider a closed macroscopic quantum system in a pure state $ψ$ evolving unitarily with Hamiltonian $H$ in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathscr{H}$. Following von Neumann, we assume a decomposition of $\mathscr{H}$ into mutually orthogonal subspaces $\mathscr{H}_ν$, where each $ν$ represents a macro state, and $\mathscr{H}_ν$ contains the pure states compatible with $ν$. We define the quantum Boltzmann entropy for a macro state $ν$ as $S_\mathrm{qB}(ν) = k_{\mathrm{B}} \log \dim \mathscr{H}_ν$, where $k_\mathrm{B}$ is the Boltzmann constant. Goldstein et al. [http://arxiv.org/abs/1903.11870] have suggested, as a version of the second law of thermodynamics, that $S_\mathrm{qB}$ predominantly increases with time for realistic macroscopic systems. Here, we discuss precise versions of this statement and confirm them for several simple models of $H$ and $\mathscr{H}_ν$.
summary: This paper investigates the emergence of the Second Law of Thermodynamics in closed quantum systems by analyzing the increase of quantum Boltzmann entropy. Using concepts like macro state decomposition and probability currents, the authors confirm the second law for various models, suggesting that irreversible behavior arises naturally from unitary quantum dynamics in the macroscopic limit.
main_problem: The paper addresses the formulation and confirmation of precise versions of the second law of thermodynamics for closed macroscopic quantum systems.
main_result: The authors confirm that the quantum Boltzmann entropy ($S_{qB}$) tends to increase over time for several simple models, suggesting the emergence of thermodynamic laws in isolated quantum evolution.
method: The analysis uses theoretical frameworks involving the decomposition of the Hilbert space into macro states and analyzing the time evolution of probability distributions and quantum currents.
